examples.ko: 부장님 출장 때문에 일등석 표를 알아보고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking into first-class tickets for the manager's business trip.
First class has wide seats and good service.

examples.ko: 비싸서 저는 일등석을 한 번도 못 타 봤어요.
examples.en: It's expensive, so I've never ridden in first class.
This train has no separate first class.

examples.ko: 친구가 일등석에 앉아서 사진을 보내 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend sat in first class and sent me a photo.

examples.ko: 일등석으로 바꾸려면 돈을 얼마나 더 내야 해요?
examples.en: How much more do I have to pay to switch to first class?

explain: 비행기에서는 '퍼스트클래스'라고도 해요. 그 아래 등급은 '비즈니스석', '이코노미석'처럼 불러요. '일등석에 앉다'처럼 자리에는 '에'를 써요.
explain_en: On planes it is also called 'first class'. The lower classes are called '비즈니스석' (business) and '이코노미석' (economy). Use '에' for the seat you sit in, as in '일등석에 앉다'.

examples.ko: 이 골목은 일방통행이라서 반대로 들어가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: This alley is one-way, so you can't enter from the other side.

examples.ko: 일방통행 표지판을 못 보고 그냥 들어갔어요.
examples.en: I didn't see the one-way sign and just drove in.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 도로가 다음 달부터 일방통행으로 바뀌어요.
examples.en: The road in our neighborhood becomes one-way from next month.
This is a one-way street, but a taxi came the wrong way.

examples.ko: 일방통행 길이라 한참 돌아서 가야 해요.
examples.en: It's a one-way street, so we have to go around for a long way.

examples.ko: 길이 일방통행이 아닌지 먼저 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: First check whether the street is one-way.

explain: 도로 표지판에는 '일방통행'이라고 쓰여 있고, 말로는 '일방통행 길'이라고 해요. 반대로 양쪽으로 다니는 길은 '양방향'이라고 해요. 대화나 관계가 한쪽으로만 흐를 때도 비유로 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 한 사람만 말하고 상대의 말은 듣지 않을 때 비판하는 느낌으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used critically when only one person talks and the other's words are not heard.

explain_en: Road signs say '일방통행', and in speech people say '일방통행 길' (a one-way street). A road that goes both ways is '양방향'. It is also used figuratively when a conversation or relationship only goes in one direction.

examples.en: At home I wear comfortable everyday clothes.

examples.ko: 이 원피스는 일상복으로 입기에 딱 좋아요.
examples.en: This dress is just right to wear day to day.

examples.ko: 일상복 브랜드에서 세일을 해서 티셔츠를 샀어요.
examples.en: An everyday-wear brand was on sale, so I bought a T-shirt.

examples.ko: 출근할 때도 일상복 차림으로 다녀도 돼요?
examples.en: Is it okay to go to work in everyday clothes too?

examples.ko: 한복을 일상복처럼 입는 사람도 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More people are wearing hanbok like everyday clothes.

examples.ko: 일상복이 너무 낡아서 새로 사야 해요.
examples.en: My everyday clothes are so worn out that I need to buy new ones.

explain: '평상복'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. 반대로 격식 있는 자리의 옷은 '정장'이나 '예복'이라고 해요. 한복을 평소에 입기 편하게 만든 옷은 '생활한복'이라고 불러요.
explain_en: It is used almost the same as '평상복' (casual wear). The opposite is formal wear such as '정장' or '예복'. Hanbok redesigned for daily comfort is called '생활한복'.

examples.en: Today is our shop's first anniversary.

examples.ko: 결혼 일주년을 맞아 여행을 가기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to take a trip for our first wedding anniversary.
I was invited to the company's first-anniversary event.
I made the first-anniversary cake myself.
It's our first anniversary, so every menu item is discounted.
My first year at the company is already approaching.

explain: 숫자로 '1주년'이라고 많이 쓰고 읽을 때는 [일쭈년]이에요. 가게나 회사의 기념일에는 '개업 1주년', '창립 1주년'처럼 앞에 말을 붙여요. 아기의 첫 생일은 '돌'이라고 하고 '일주년'이라고는 하지 않아요.
explain_en: It is often written with a number as '1주년' and read [일쭈년]. For shops and companies you add a word before it, like '개업 1주년' or '창립 1주년'. A baby's first birthday is called '돌', not '일주년'.

en: deposit amount; payment on an account

examples.en: Check your account to see whether the deposit amount is right.
The deposit will arrive in the account today.
I wrote the deposit amount wrong by mistake.
Please email me the deposit confirmation.
The interest changes depending on the deposit amount.
Points are added automatically in proportion to the deposit amount.

explain: '금액'은 돈의 양이고 '입금액'은 계좌에 넣은 돈이에요. 반대는 '출금액'이고, 들어온 돈과 나간 돈을 같이 볼 때 짝으로 써요. 말할 때는 '입금한 돈'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: '금액' is an amount of money, and '입금액' is the money put into an account. The opposite is '출금액', and the two are used as a pair when looking at money in and out. In speech people also say '입금한 돈'.

examples.ko: 시험 전에 외운 단어를 입속으로 중얼거리고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm muttering the words I memorized before the test under my breath.

examples.ko: 면접 전에 준비한 말을 입속으로 계속 되뇌었어요.
examples.en: Before the interview I kept repeating my prepared words to myself.
The candy melts smoothly in my mouth.

examples.ko: 입속이 말라서 물을 한 모금 마셨어요.
examples.en: My mouth was dry, so I took a sip of water.
The dentist examined the inside of my mouth carefully.
I burned the inside of my mouth eating hot soup.

explain: '입안'과 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. '입속으로 중얼거리다'처럼 소리를 거의 내지 않고 말할 때도 자주 써요. 이때는 '속으로'가 남에게 들리지 않게 하는 느낌을 줘요.
explain_en: It is used almost the same as '입안'. It also appears in '입속으로 중얼거리다', to speak with hardly any sound. There, '속으로' gives the feeling that others can't hear it.

en: student preparing for an entrance exam

examples.en: Exam-prep students go to cram school even during vacation.
Last year I was an entrance-exam student.

examples.ko: 입시생 자녀를 둔 부모님은 걱정이 많아요.
examples.en: Parents with a child preparing for entrance exams worry a lot.
The library is full of students preparing for exams.

examples.ko: 입시생에게는 마지막 한 달이 가장 중요해요.
examples.en: For exam-prep students the final month is the most important.

examples.ko: 입시생을 위한 간식 세트를 팔고 있어요.
examples.en: They're selling snack sets for students preparing for exams.

explain: 대학 입시를 준비하는 학생을 말해요. '수험생'은 입시뿐 아니라 자격시험 등 다른 시험을 준비하는 사람까지 넓게 가리켜요. 입시를 한 번 더 준비하는 사람은 '재수생'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a student preparing for university entrance exams. '수험생' is broader and includes people preparing for any exam, such as certifications. Someone retaking the entrance exam is called a '재수생'.

examples.en: My grandmother is in a room on the third floor.

examples.ko: 입원실이 조용해서 푹 쉴 수 있어요.
examples.en: The hospital room is quiet, so I can rest well.

examples.ko: 입원실에서는 큰 소리로 전화하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not talk loudly on the phone in the patient room.
The hospital bed was uncomfortable, so I slept badly.
The nurse brought my medicine to the room.
I told them I'd like to change rooms.

explain: '병실'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 입원실은 병원 안내문이나 서류에서 많이 보이는 말이에요. 여러 사람이 함께 쓰는 방은 '다인실', 혼자 쓰는 방은 '1인실'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '병실' means the same thing. '입원실' is a word you often see in hospital notices and paperwork. A shared room is '다인실' and a private room is '1인실'.

examples.en: A gravel path is uncomfortable to walk on, so I wore sneakers.
Riding a bike on a gravel path shakes you a lot.
The country gravel path gets slippery when it rains.

examples.ko: 자갈길 끝에 작은 집이 한 채 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small house at the end of the gravel path.
It's hard to go along a gravel path in high heels.
The car rattled as it passed over the gravel path.

explain: 길 앞에 바탕이 되는 말을 붙여 '흙길', '눈길', '빗길', '산길'처럼 길의 종류를 말해요. 자갈길도 그중 하나예요. '자갈길을 걷다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 써요.
explain_en: Korean puts the surface or setting before 길 to name a type of road, such as '흙길', '눈길', '빗길' and '산길'. 자갈길 is one of these. It goes with '을/를', as in '자갈길을 걷다'.

examples.ko: 자동문 앞에 서면 문이 저절로 열려요.
examples.en: If you stand in front of the automatic door, it opens by itself.

examples.ko: 자동문이 고장 나서 지금은 수동으로 열어야 해요.
examples.en: The automatic door is broken, so now we have to open it by hand.

examples.ko: 아기가 자동문에 손이 끼지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful that the baby's hand doesn't get caught in the automatic door.

examples.ko: 마트 입구는 자동문이라서 카트를 밀고 들어가기 편해요.
examples.en: The store entrance is an automatic door, so it's easy to push a cart in.
A cold wind blew as soon as I passed the automatic door.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 자동문이 아니라서 문을 직접 밀어야 해요.
examples.en: This building has no automatic door, so you have to push the door yourself.

explain: '자동문이 열리다/닫히다'처럼 문이 스스로 움직일 때는 '열리다·닫히다'를 써요. 사람이 직접 여는 건 '열다'예요. 고장 났을 때는 '수동으로 열다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: When the door moves by itself, use '열리다/닫히다', as in '자동문이 열리다'. When a person opens it, use '열다'. When it is broken, you say '수동으로 열다' (open it manually).

examples.en: The market in our neighborhood is a big source of pride.

examples.ko: 자랑거리는 많은데 겸손해서 말을 안 해요.
examples.en: He has plenty to boast about but is modest and doesn't say it.
The only thing I can be proud of is being diligent.

examples.ko: 이 상은 우리 가족의 자랑거리로 남을 거예요.
examples.en: This award will remain a source of pride for our family.
Tell us your achievements to be proud of, one by one.

examples.ko: 남에게 보여 줄 만한 자랑거리가 생겼어요.
examples.en: I now have something worth showing off to others.

explain: '자랑하다'는 행동이고 '자랑거리'는 자랑할 대상이에요. 사람이 느끼는 마음은 '자랑스럽다'로 말해요. '이야깃거리', '걱정거리'처럼 '-거리'가 붙은 말이 많아요.
explain_en: '자랑하다' is the act of boasting, while '자랑거리' is the thing to boast about. The feeling a person has is '자랑스럽다'. Many words take '-거리', like '이야깃거리' and '걱정거리'.

examples.ko: 오늘 선생님이 안 계셔서 자습을 했어요.
examples.en: The teacher wasn't here today, so we had self-study.

examples.ko: 야간 자습이 끝나고 집에 가면 열 시예요.
examples.en: When I get home after evening self-study, it's ten o'clock.
You have to be quiet during self-study time.
Studying alone is hard, so I go to a cram school.

examples.ko: 수업이 갑자기 자습으로 바뀌어서 다들 좋아했어요.
examples.en: The class suddenly turned into self-study, and everyone was happy.
During vacation I study by myself at the library.

explain: 학교에서 선생님이 가르치지 않고 학생이 스스로 공부하는 시간을 '자습 시간'이라고 해요. '자습을 시키다'는 선생님 입장, '자습하다'는 학생 입장에서 써요. 선생님 없이 혼자 배우는 것은 '독학'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: At school, a period where students study on their own without a teacher teaching is called '자습 시간'. '자습을 시키다' is from the teacher's side and '자습하다' from the student's. Learning alone without a teacher can also be called '독학'.

examples.en: I found a small place to rent near the university.

examples.ko: 자취방이 좁아서 책상을 놓을 자리가 없어요.
examples.en: My room is small, so there's no space for a desk.
My friends came over to my place.

examples.ko: 자취방 월세가 한 달에 오십만 원이에요.
examples.en: The monthly rent for my room is 500,000 won.
I cooked and ate ramyeon in my room.
A rented room is good when it gets plenty of sunlight.

explain: '자취하다'는 밥과 빨래를 직접 하며 혼자 사는 거예요. 밥을 챙겨 주는 '하숙'과 달라요. 건물 형태로는 '원룸'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: '자취하다' means living alone and doing your own cooking and laundry. It differs from '하숙', where meals are provided. By building type it can also be called a '원룸'.

examples.en: Who is the composer of this song?
The composer played it himself on the piano.

examples.ko: 저는 유명한 작곡자를 만나서 사인을 받았어요.
examples.en: I met a famous composer and got an autograph.
The composer and the lyricist are the same person.

examples.ko: 작곡자 이름이 앨범 뒷면에 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The composer's name is written on the back of the album.
I asked the composer for a song, but there's no reply.

explain: '작곡가'와 거의 같은데, 직업을 말할 때는 '작곡가'가 더 자연스러워요. 곡을 만든 사람 한 명을 가리킬 때 '작곡자'를 써요. 가사를 쓴 사람은 '작사가/작사자'예요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '작곡가', but for a profession '작곡가' sounds more natural. '작곡자' points to the person who made a particular piece. The person who wrote the lyrics is '작사가' or '작사자'.

examples.en: I share a room with my second older sister.
My second older sister is in graduate school.

examples.ko: 작은누나가 제 생일에 책을 선물해 줬어요.
examples.en: My second older sister gave me a book for my birthday.
I called my second older sister and asked about the homework.
Thanks to my second older sister, I came to like English.
My eldest sister is married, and my second sister is still a student.

explain: 남자가 누나가 둘 이상일 때 둘째 누나를 '작은누나', 첫째를 '큰누나'라고 불러요. '작은'은 키가 작다는 뜻이 아니라 순서를 나타내요. 여자가 부를 때는 '누나' 대신 '언니'를 써요.
explain_en: A man with two or more older sisters calls the second '작은누나' and the first '큰누나'. '작은' here is about order, not height. A woman uses '언니' instead of '누나'.

examples.ko: 큰딸은 직장 때문에 서울에 살고, 작은딸은 부모님과 같이 살아요.
examples.en: The older daughter lives in Seoul for work, and the younger daughter lives with her parents.
My younger daughter entered university this year.
I plan to buy my younger daughter a different present.
I took my younger daughter to the hospital and came back.
The family gathered for my younger daughter's birthday.
Because of my younger daughter, mornings are noisy.

explain: 딸이 둘일 때 둘째 딸을 '작은딸', 첫째를 '큰딸'이라고 불러요. '작은'은 크기가 아니라 순서를 말해요. 딸이 셋 이상이면 '둘째 딸', '막내딸'처럼 순서나 위치로 말해요.
explain_en: With two daughters, the second is '작은딸' and the first is '큰딸'. '작은' is about order, not size. With three or more, you say '둘째 딸' or '막내딸' by order or position.

examples.en: My second older sister is two years older than me.
My second older sister borrowed my clothes.
My second older sister also graduated from the same school.
I'm closest to my second older sister.
I confided my worries to my second older sister.
I sang at my second older sister's wedding.

explain: 여자가 언니가 둘 이상일 때 둘째 언니를 '작은언니'라고 해요. '작은'은 키가 작다는 뜻이 아니라 순서예요. 첫째는 '큰언니'예요.
explain_en: A woman with two or more older sisters calls the second one '작은언니'. '작은' means order here, not short height. The eldest is '큰언니'.

examples.en: My second older brother has served in the military.
My second older brother gave me pocket money.
I play soccer with my second older brother.
I borrowed a laptop from my second older brother.
Thanks to my second older brother, I started preparing for a job.
I take after my second older brother, so I sing well too.

explain: 형이 둘일 때 둘째 형을 '작은형', 첫째를 '큰형'이라고 해요. 크기가 아니라 순서를 말해요. 여동생이 부를 때는 '형' 대신 '오빠'를 써서 '작은오빠'라고 해요.
explain_en: With two older brothers, the second is '작은형' and the first is '큰형'. It is about order, not size. A younger sister says '오빠' instead of '형', so '작은오빠'.

examples.ko: 동생은 주말마다 열두 시까지 자는 잠꾸러기예요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is a sleepyhead who sleeps until noon every weekend.
I'm a sleepyhead, so I'm always late for morning appointments.
My son is a sleepyhead, so he's hard to wake up.
Hey sleepyhead, get up now!

examples.ko: 저는 잠꾸러기가 아니고 밤에 일하는 사람이에요.
examples.en: I'm not a sleepyhead, I'm someone who works at night.
I found out after marriage that my husband is a sleepyhead.

explain: 잠이 많은 사람을 귀엽게 놀릴 때 써요. 아이나 가까운 사이에 쓰고, 어른에게 직접 말하면 무례할 수 있어요. '장난꾸러기', '욕심꾸러기'처럼 '-꾸러기'가 붙은 말도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used to tease someone affectionately for sleeping a lot. Use it with children or close people; saying it directly to an adult can be rude. Other words with '-꾸러기' include '장난꾸러기' and '욕심꾸러기'.

examples.ko: 남편은 잠버릇이 나빠서 자꾸 이불을 걷어차요.
examples.en: My husband has a bad sleeping habit and keeps kicking off the blanket.

examples.ko: 제 잠버릇은 잘 때 이를 가는 거래요.
examples.en: They say my sleeping habit is grinding my teeth.

examples.ko: 아이의 잠버릇 때문에 침대 가장자리에 쿠션을 놓았어요.
examples.en: Because of my child's sleeping habits, I put cushions at the bed's edge.

examples.ko: 룸메이트의 잠버릇을 알고 나서 귀마개를 샀어요.
examples.en: After learning my roommate's sleeping habits, I bought earplugs.
I asked my family about my sleeping habits.
Even the way he sleeps is just like his dad's.

explain: 잠잘 때 나오는 습관을 말해요. '잠버릇이 나쁘다/고약하다/심하다'처럼 문제가 되는 습관을 말할 때 많이 써요. '이를 갈다', '이불을 걷어차다', '잠꼬대를 하다'가 대표적인 잠버릇이에요.
explain_en: It refers to habits that show up while sleeping. It is often used for problem habits, as in '잠버릇이 나쁘다/고약하다/심하다'. Typical examples are '이를 갈다' (grind teeth), '이불을 걷어차다' (kick off the blanket) and '잠꼬대를 하다' (talk in one's sleep).

examples.ko: 할머니, 이 반찬도 좀 잡숫고 가세요.
examples.en: Grandmother, please have some of this side dish before you go.

examples.ko: 아버지는 아침마다 죽을 잡숫는 습관이 있으세요.
examples.en: My father has a habit of eating porridge every morning.

examples.ko: 너무 짜게 잡숫지 마세요. 건강에 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Please don't eat food that's too salty. It's bad for your health.
If there's anything you'd like to eat, please tell me.

examples.ko: 손님이 잡숫기 편하게 고기를 잘라 드렸어요.
examples.en: I cut the meat so it would be easy for the guest to eat.
It's lovely to see you eating so heartily.

explain: '드시다'와 함께 '먹다'의 높임말이에요. 높일 때는 '잡수세요', '잡수셨어요'처럼 형태가 바뀌어요. 나 자신이나 아랫사람에게는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Along with '드시다', it is an honorific for '먹다'. The honorific forms change shape, as in '잡수세요' and '잡수셨어요'. Never use it for yourself or for someone younger.

examples.en: At work, newcomers usually start by learning odd jobs.
I did nothing but odd jobs all day and then left work.

examples.ko: 잡일이 많아서 정작 중요한 일을 못 했어요.
examples.en: There were so many odd jobs that I couldn't do the really important work.
I earn pocket money helping with odd jobs at a restaurant.

examples.ko: 청소나 심부름 같은 잡일은 제가 할게요.
examples.en: I'll do the odd jobs like cleaning and errands.
Odd jobs are taking up too much of my time.

explain: 특별한 기술이 필요 없는 자잘한 일을 가리켜요. 약간 낮춰 보는 느낌이 있어서 남이 하는 일에 쓰면 실례일 수 있어요. 비슷한 말로 '허드렛일'이 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to small tasks that need no special skill. It carries a slightly belittling tone, so using it for someone else's work can be rude. A similar word is '허드렛일'.

examples.en: I read a magazine in the hospital waiting room.

examples.ko: 이 잡지책은 매달 첫째 주에 나와요.
examples.en: This magazine comes out in the first week of every month.

examples.ko: 서점에서 패션 잡지책을 한 권 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a fashion magazine at the bookstore.
The photos in the magazine are so pretty.
Magazines are piled up on the desk.

examples.ko: 이번 달 잡지책에 제 글이 실렸어요.
examples.en: My writing was published in this month's magazine.

explain: '잡지'와 같은 뜻이에요. 보통 '잡지를 읽다'처럼 쓰고, 종이로 된 것을 말할 때 '잡지책'이라고도 해요. 정기적으로 나오는 것은 '월간지', '주간지'라고 불러요.
explain_en: It means the same as '잡지'. People usually say '잡지를 읽다', and '잡지책' is also used for the printed paper version. Regularly published ones are called '월간지' (monthly) or '주간지' (weekly).

examples.en: My uncle is getting married next month.

examples.ko: 아들이 장가갈 나이가 됐는데 연애도 안 해요.
examples.en: My son is of marrying age, but he isn't even dating.
I was the MC on the day my friend got married.

examples.ko: 형은 작년에 장가가서 지금 신혼집에 살아요.
examples.en: My older brother got married last year and now lives in their newlywed home.
I'm going to save money before I get married.
After getting married, I felt more responsible.

explain: 남자가 결혼한다는 뜻으로만 써요. 여자가 결혼할 때는 '시집가다'라고 했지만, 요즘은 남녀 모두 '결혼하다'가 가장 무난해요. 어른들이 농담처럼 '장가 언제 가니?'라고 묻기도 해요.
explain_en: It is used only for a man marrying. For a woman the old word is '시집가다', but today '결혼하다' is the safest for everyone. Elders sometimes ask jokingly, '장가 언제 가니?' (When are you getting married?).

examples.en: That child's face is full of mischief.
He looked at me with playful eyes.
Even as he gets older, his playfulness stays the same.
My younger sibling often gets scolded for being mischievous.
She answered the phone in a playful voice.

examples.ko: 장난기가 발동해서 친구를 깜짝 놀라게 했어요.
examples.en: My playful side kicked in and I gave my friend a surprise.

explain: '장난기가 많다/가득하다/있다'로 자주 써요. '장난기가 발동하다'처럼 말하면 갑자기 장난치고 싶어지는 상황을 가리켜요. 나쁜 뜻이 아니라 귀엽거나 유쾌한 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is often used as '장난기가 많다/가득하다/있다'. '장난기가 발동하다' describes suddenly feeling like playing a prank. It is not negative; it feels cute or cheerful.

examples.ko: 장인어른은 사위가 창업한다고 하자 처음에는 말리셨어요.
examples.en: When his son-in-law said he would start a business, his father-in-law at first tried to stop him.
The father-in-law and son-in-law go fishing together.
At the holiday I gave my father-in-law some spending money.

examples.ko: 장인어른이 직접 담근 김치를 보내 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father-in-law sent me kimchi he made himself.

examples.ko: 처음 장인어른을 뵈러 가던 날 너무 떨렸어요.
examples.en: I was so nervous the day I first went to meet my father-in-law.
The whole family gathered for my father-in-law's birthday.

explain: 아내의 아버지를 높여 부르는 말이에요. 직접 부를 때는 보통 '아버님'이라고 해요. 남편의 아버지는 '시아버지'이고, 부를 때는 마찬가지로 '아버님'이에요.
explain_en: It is a respectful word for one's wife's father. When addressing him directly, people usually say '아버님'. A husband's father is '시아버지', also addressed as '아버님'.

examples.ko: 엄마가 해 주신 장조림이 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: The jangjorim my mom makes is the tastiest.
Jangjorim is just right as a side dish for rice.
I asked them to pack jangjorim in my lunchbox.

examples.ko: 장조림 국물에 밥을 비벼 먹으면 맛있어요.
examples.en: Rice mixed with jangjorim broth is delicious.
I tried making jangjorim with quail eggs.

examples.ko: 장조림을 만들 때는 간장을 넉넉히 넣어요.
examples.en: When making jangjorim, I add plenty of soy sauce.

explain: '-조림'은 '감자조림', '고등어조림'처럼 졸인 반찬에 붙는 말이에요. 장조림은 짭짤해서 밥에 얹어 먹거나 비벼 먹어요. 소고기 말고 메추리알이나 두부를 넣기도 해요.
explain_en: '-조림' is attached to braised side dishes, like '감자조림' and '고등어조림'. Jangjorim is salty, so people eat it over rice or mixed into it. Besides beef, quail eggs or tofu are sometimes added.

examples.ko: 계획에 허점이 보여서 전체를 재검토해야 해요.
examples.en: I saw gaps in the plan, so we have to review all of it again.

examples.ko: 이 결정은 재검토할 여지가 있다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think there is room to reconsider this decision.

examples.ko: 내일까지 예산안을 한 번 더 재검토해 주세요.
examples.en: Please review the budget proposal once more by tomorrow.
The team leader told me to review the report again.
Before submitting, I carefully rechecked the numbers.

examples.ko: 문제가 계속 생겨서 계약 조건을 재검토하기로 했어요.
examples.en: Problems kept arising, so we decided to reconsider the contract terms.

explain: 이미 정한 일을 다시 따져 볼 때 써요. '다시 재검토하다'는 '재'와 '다시'가 겹쳐서 어색해요. '재검토 중이다', '재검토가 필요하다'처럼 명사로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: Use it when taking another look at something already decided. '다시 재검토하다' sounds odd because '재' and '다시' both mean 'again'. It is also often used as a noun, as in '재검토 중이다' or '재검토가 필요하다'.

examples.ko: 그 물건은 몇몇 재래시장에서만 구할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can only find that item at a few traditional markets.

examples.ko: 어머니는 생필품을 살 때 재래시장보다 슈퍼를 더 자주 이용하세요.
examples.en: When buying daily necessities, my mother uses supermarkets more than traditional markets.
On the weekend I bought fresh vegetables at the traditional market.

examples.ko: 재래시장은 값을 깎을 수 있어서 좋아요.
examples.en: I like traditional markets because you can bargain.
The traditional market in our neighborhood got renovated.
I went to see a traditional market with a foreign friend.

explain: 마트에서는 값이 정해져 있지만 재래시장에서는 깎아 달라고 말하기도 해요. '전통시장'도 거의 같은 뜻으로 써요. 마트·백화점과 짝으로 비교해서 말할 때가 많아요.
explain_en: Prices are fixed at marts, but at a traditional market people sometimes ask for a discount. '전통시장' is used with almost the same meaning. It is often contrasted with marts and department stores.

examples.en: My grade was low, so I'm retaking that course.

examples.ko: 재수강하면 성적을 다시 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you retake the course, you can get a new grade.

examples.ko: 재수강 신청 기간이 이번 주 금요일까지예요.
examples.en: The retake registration period is until this Friday.
Do I have to pay extra tuition to retake a course?
I'm planning to retake a class I took last year.
My friend's graduation was delayed because of a retaken course.

explain: 대학에서 이미 들은 과목을 다시 들을 때 써요. '재수강하다'나 '재수강을 하다'로 말해요. 입시를 다시 준비하는 '재수'와 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It is used at university when taking a course you have already taken. You say '재수강하다' or '재수강을 하다'. Don't confuse it with '재수', retaking the entrance exam.

examples.en: I recycled old clothes into a bag.
Plastic can only be recycled if you sort it.
This paper cup is hard to recycle.
Don't throw the bottle away; try reusing it.
Our shop reuses packaging boxes.
The souvenir is a bag made of recycled fabric.

explain: '재활용품', '재활용 쓰레기', '재활용 센터'처럼 앞말로도 많이 써요. 쓰레기를 종류별로 나눠 버리는 건 '분리수거'라고 해요. 일상에서는 '다시 쓰다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is often used before another noun, as in '재활용품', '재활용 쓰레기' and '재활용 센터'. Sorting trash by type is called '분리수거'. In daily talk people also say '다시 쓰다'.

en: money bank; coin bank; piggy bank

examples.en: I put coins into the piggy bank.
The piggy bank was full, so I took it to the bank.

examples.ko: 아이가 저금통을 열어 동전을 세어 봤어요.
examples.en: The child opened the piggy bank and counted the coins.
I bought a present with the money in my piggy bank.
My younger sibling saves spare change in the coin bank.
Coins came tumbling out of the piggy bank.

explain: 돼지 모양이 많아서 '돼지 저금통'이라고 자주 말해요. 동전을 모은 저금통을 비울 때 '털다'라고 말하기도 해요. 은행에 돈을 맡길 때는 '저금통'이 아니라 '통장'을 써요.
explain_en: Many are pig-shaped, so people often say '돼지 저금통'. When emptying a full coin bank, people sometimes say '털다'. For saving at a bank, you use a '통장' (passbook), not a 저금통.

en: groceries for dinner; foods for dinner

examples.en: On my way home from work I bought dinner groceries at the mart.
There's nothing for dinner in the fridge.
What should we get for dinner tonight?

examples.ko: 시장에서 저녁거리로 생선을 한 마리 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a fish at the market for dinner.

examples.ko: 저녁거리 걱정 때문에 일찍 집에 가요.
examples.en: I'm going home early because I'm worried about dinner.

examples.ko: 저녁거리 좀 사 오는 길에 전화할게요.
examples.en: I'll call you on my way back from buying dinner stuff.

explain: 저녁밥을 만들 재료를 말해요. 완성된 음식보다 재료 쪽이라 '저녁거리를 사다/장보다'처럼 써요. '반찬거리', '국거리'처럼 '-거리'가 붙은 말이 많아요.
explain_en: It means the ingredients for making dinner. It leans toward ingredients rather than finished food, so you say '저녁거리를 사다' or shop for it. Many words take '-거리', like '반찬거리' and '국거리'.

examples.en: A west-facing living room is nice because the evening glow is beautiful.
I walked along the riverside watching the sunset glow.
The sky was dyed red by the evening glow.
We took photos under the evening glow.

examples.ko: 저녁노을은 날씨가 맑은 날 더 예뻐요.
examples.en: The evening glow is prettier on clear days.
The evening glow is settling over the sea.

explain: '노을'만 써도 되고, '저녁노을'은 해가 질 때라는 점을 분명히 해요. 아침에 보이는 노을은 '아침노을'이라고 해요. '노을이 지다', '노을이 물들다'가 어울리는 짝이에요.
explain_en: '노을' alone is fine; '저녁노을' makes clear it is at sunset. The glow seen in the morning is '아침노을'. Natural pairings are '노을이 지다' and '노을이 물들다'.

examples.ko: 자기 전에 적당량의 물을 마시는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's good to drink a suitable amount of water before sleeping.
Add only the right amount of salt so it isn't salty.
Please take the medicine in the proper amount.
The right amount differs a little from person to person.
The recipe just says 'right amount', so I'm confused.

examples.ko: 비료를 적당량 뿌려 주면 화초가 잘 자라요.
examples.en: If you sprinkle the right amount of fertilizer, plants grow well.

explain: '적당히'는 부사라서 '적당히 넣다'처럼 쓰고, '적당량'은 '적당량을 넣다'처럼 명사로 써요. 레시피에 '소금 적당량'이라고 적혀 있으면 정해진 숫자 없이 맛을 보며 넣으라는 안내예요. '알맞은 양'으로 풀어 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: '적당히' is an adverb, as in '적당히 넣다', while '적당량' is a noun, as in '적당량을 넣다'. If a recipe says '소금 적당량', there is no fixed number, so you add salt while tasting. It can also be spelled out as '알맞은 양'.

examples.en: We bought a new rice cooker for our newlywed home.

examples.ko: 전기밥솥이 밥이 다 됐다고 알려 줘요.
examples.en: The rice cooker tells me the rice is done.
You can also steam food with a rice cooker.

examples.ko: 전기밥솥에 쌀과 물을 넣고 취사 버튼을 눌렀어요.
examples.en: I put rice and water in the rice cooker and pressed the cook button.
This rice cooker keeps food warm for a long time.

examples.ko: 전기밥솥 뚜껑을 열자 김이 확 올라왔어요.
examples.en: When I opened the rice cooker lid, steam rushed up.

explain: 일상에서는 그냥 '밥솥'이라고 해도 통해요. 버튼은 '취사'(밥 짓기)와 '보온'(따뜻하게 두기)이 기본이에요. 밥을 '짓다'라고 하는 점도 함께 알아 두세요.
explain_en: In daily life, just saying '밥솥' also works. The basic buttons are '취사' (cook) and '보온' (keep warm). Also note that rice is 'made' with the verb '짓다'.

examples.en: In winter I sleep with the electric mat on.
If the electric mat is too hot, lower the temperature.

examples.ko: 전기장판 위에 누우면 몸이 사르르 풀려요.
examples.en: When I lie on the electric mat, my body relaxes.

examples.ko: 할머니 방에 새 전기장판을 깔아 드렸어요.
examples.en: I laid a new electric mat in Grandmother's room.
It's dangerous to leave an electric mat on for a long time.
Thanks to the electric mat, I run the boiler less.

explain: '전기요'라고도 해요. '켜다/끄다', '깔다'와 함께 써요. 오래 켜 두고 자면 저온 화상을 입을 수 있어서 조심하라는 말을 자주 들어요.
explain_en: It is also called '전기요'. It goes with '켜다/끄다' (turn on/off) and '깔다' (lay out). You often hear warnings to be careful, since sleeping on it for long can cause low-temperature burns.
